chapter: Chick Webb, Lucky Roberts, Alex Jackson
title: Conflicts between Chick Webb and gigs; sending subs
summary: Scott describes juggling contracts and sending substitutes.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: You went with Chick, you joined Chick then.

Yeah, yeah. Well, I stayed with him awhile. But all the time, I was getting off and coming in there and all like that, sometimes it was really annoying, because you can't break a contract when you're playing with one and the other, and this guy wants you to play so-and-so, and you can't do it. I couldn't do it. It really used to get on my nerves, sometimes. Sometimes I'd have two gigs a night, and I'd go around the Rhythm Club and I'd find a trumpet player that wasn't working that night. Call up the guy and tell him I couldn't make it but I'm sending a good guy in my place. And they couldn't say anything about it. But, you
know what I mean? You couldn't work all that -- it was too much work. How could I work two places? The union wouldn't allow it, and how could I possibly do it?
